newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline off after rising on refinery fire.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline off after rising on refinery fire.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline fell Wednesday morning giving up earlier gains stoked by a fire at Tosco's Avon refinery in California late Tuesday night, traders.

"The fire really spooked the market, but it hasn't turned the market around for good," said Mike DeLuca, trader with Prudential Securities, adding that in reality the fire should have little effect on supply.

At 1133 EST, February gasoline was off 0.08 cent a gallon at 65.95 cents after rising to 68.50 cents earlier. An explosion at a hydrocracker unit set Tosco's Avon oil refinery ablaze. The refinery has capacity of 150,000 barrels a day.
The cause of the explosion and fire was unknown and it was too soon to estimate damage or whether the incident would disrupt operations, a Tosco spokesman said.
Before the fire, Tosco had shut a 42,000 bpd coker at the refinery for 35 days for planned maintenance.
February heating oil was up 0.02 cent a gallon at 66.05 cents, and March crude was off 26 cents at $23.96 a barrel.

"There is talk of a lot of imports, and that the cash market has really come off after the February expiry," said a New York crude dealer, noting the Feb contract left the board to meet plenty of supply.
After the market's close, the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected to release oil inventory data for the week ended January 17.
Dealers said heating oil was being supported by expectations that last week's colder temperatures caused a draw in distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel.
Preliminary estimates called for a draw of two to three million barrels in those stocks. Imports were expected to have increased crude and gasoline stocks modestly.

Prompt crude had broken $24.00 support by midday, but trendline support was pegged at around $23.50, with the line extending from the March low on July 29 of $18.37 and extending through the low December 11 of $22.20.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
